# Midterm 2 Instructions

Midterm 2 consists of **two parts**:

1.  **Take-Home Data Analysis (Preparation Component)**
2.  **In-Class Exam (Application Component)**

Both components are required.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Part 1: Take-Home Data Analysis

## Objective

You will examine and analyze the provided dataset using the statistical methods covered in class. This portion assesses your ability to conduct appropriate analyses and generate correct outputs.

## Collaboration Policy

-   You may work together with classmates **ONLY FOR THE TAKE-HOME PORTION** of the exam.
-   The **in-class exam is in-person and individual.**

Each student must fully understand the work and be prepared to independently explain, justify, and interpret their results during the in-class exam.

## Use of AI Tools

You **do not need to use AI tools** for this assignment.

All required code is already available in:

-   Lab assignments

-   Lab slides

-   Investigation assignments

These materials contain everything you need.

You **may use AI tools only if you clearly understand the code AI generates.**

You are responsible for:

-   Ensuring the code is correct

-   Being able to explain the results during the in-class portion

If you cannot explain your results, it may negatively affect your in-class performance.

## Software Guidelines

You will use **both R and the applet** for this exam.

### Use **R** for:

-   Data visualization
-   Data exploration
-   One-sample t-test (optional — may also use applet)
-   Independent samples t-test (optional — may also use applet)
-   Paired samples t-test (optional — may also use applet)

### Use the **Applet** for:

-   Two proportions z-test

If **R is not working on your computer**, you may use the applet instead for every item.

## Required Analyses

You must complete the following (as applicable to the dataset):

-   Data visualization
-   Data exploration
-   One-sample t-test
-   Independent samples t-test
-   Paired samples t-test
-   Two proportions z-test

## Deliverables (Bring to Class)

You must bring:

-   Printed outputs (graphs, tables, test results, etc.)
-   Your R code (if you used R)
-   Any relevant summaries or notes
-   Your interpretations of results

Failure to bring your outputs will significantly limit your ability to complete the in-class portion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Part 2: In-Class Exam

## Objective

During class, you will use your take-home outputs to answer questions.

You will be expected to:

-   Interpret statistical results
-   State hypotheses correctly
-   Explain conclusions in context
-   Justify methodological choices
-   Discuss assumptions and limitations

You must be able to explain the analysis you conducted.

# Academic Integrity

Although collaboration is allowed for the take-home portion, each student must fully understand their work. You are responsible for being able to explain your analyses and conclusions independently during the in-class exam.
